question: What was the name of the giant single landmass which had split to form the present continents of world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pangaea.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• According to The Continental Drift Theory, all the continents formed a single continental mass **named**** **Pangaea.
 
• Laurasia is the northern supercontinent that was formed as part of the split of the Pangaean supercontinent during the late Mesozoic era. 
 
• Gondwana was a supercontinent which existed from the Neoproterozoic until the Carboniferous. It broke into Antarctica, South America, Africa, Madagascar, Australia-New Guinea and New Zealand. 
 
• Panthalassa was a superocean which surrounded the supercontinent​ ​Pangaea.
 
• * The supercontinent, Pangaea, *began to split around **200 million years ago according to Wegner.**
